messages:
amanda: Quick sync — we need a short spec for tiered routing + quota enforcement UX. Customers want: free/pro/enterprise routing preferences, region pins, and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants when capacity hits SLOs.

jay: +1. Two parts: (1) API config format for routing policy, (2) Console UX for editing per-customer overrides.

sourav: For the API shape, I'm leaning toward an ordered list of route rules with matchers and actions. Something like:

```json
{"rules": [{"match": {"tier": "free", "region": "eu"}, "action": {"route_to": ["gptx-medium-eu", "gptx-small-eu"], "fallback": true, "weight": [80,20]}}, {"match": {"tier": "enterprise"}, "action": {"route_to": ["gptx-large", "gptx-large-intel"], "pin": true}}]}
```

sourav: Fallback=true means allow automatic downgrade to next variant when latency or queue exceeds threshold.

len: How do we enforce quotas? Do we want token-level throttles per-tier + soft-fail with 429 vs queued? Free tier should get strict quotas and fast 429s; enterprise should queue or burst to reserved capacity.

priya: Console UX: show effective policy for a customer (merged global -> org -> customer). Provide visual precedence and a simulated traffic slider so support can preview fallbacks. Also add a "what if" tester for region failover.

amanda: Good. One open debate: should fallback decision live entirely in the router (edge) or be a capability of the model pool scheduler? Router-only is simpler to reason about, but scheduler can do smoother KV-cache-aware fallbacks.

jay: Router-level fallback is necessary to avoid a hard rejection; the router can prefer cheaper variants based on policy and realtime pool health metrics (latency p95, queue length). Scheduler fallback needs cross-pool coordination which complicates Dedicated/Private deployments.

sourav: Implementation idea: router consults PolicyService + PoolHealth store. PolicyService returns ordered candidates + per-candidate min_quality_score. Router tries primary; if PoolHealth indicates high latency or unavailable, it tries next candidate. If all fail, fall back to served degraded mode (strip streaming?) or 429.

len: Token accounting: we should decrement quota at router admission time to prevent double-spend when we later fallback. That means the router needs a fast quota check (Redis-ish) with atomic decrement and a small TTL. If fallback reduces token cost (smaller model), we can reimburse difference asynchronously. Edge-case: what if primary accepted but then OOM mid-gen? We'll need post-fact reconciliation.

priya: For the Console, show two columns in the policy editor: "Routing priority" and "Quota behavior". Quota behavior options: `block`, `soft-throttle`, `queue`, `burst-reserve`. Default mapping: free -> block, pro -> soft-throttle, enterprise -> burst-reserve.

amanda: Product question: do we allow per-customer overrides of default fallback weights? I think yes but hide behind Enterprise plan. Need audit trail.

jay: Agree. Also add safety: any per-customer override that enables routing to an unverified model variant must require additional approval and a K/V tag.

ops-bot: Deploy started: policy-service v2.4 -> staging (sha: d9f3b7).

amanda: Action items: (1) sourav + jay draft the API schema and edge algorithm doc (RFC) by EOD Thurs. (2) len to prototype quota atomic op in redis and doc race conditions by next Tue. (3) priya + amanda to mock console UX + simulation by Monday. (4) ops to add pool health metrics to the observability dashboard (p95 latency, queue depth).

jay: Will include examples for region-pin + model-variant weight tuning. Also adding a `min_required_quality` field so product can avoid routing to tiny quantized variants for critical workloads.

sourav: One more: include a header in our internal API `X-Route-Decision` that records which candidate was selected and why (policy, health, quota). That will make debugging easier.

len: I'll start a small PoC repo `routing-quota-proto` and post link.

priya: UX note: add a tooltip on "fallback" that explains "Fallback attempts to route to next candidate when health or quota constraints prevent primary selection." Keep it simple for SMEs.

amanda: Great discussion. If no blockers, we'll merge RFC draft into `eng/proposals` and schedule a 30-min sync after RFC review. :thumbsup:

jay: lgtm

sourav: lgtm

ops-bot: Deploy succeeded: policy-service v2.4 -> staging (sha: d9f3b7) in 45s.
